relevance.rationale: Revisits the Dimofte-Gaiotto-Gukov construction and does two things the corpus's conj:mirror-3d-3d-correspondence directly needs. First it records a caveat: only a SUBSET of the irreducible flat SL(2,C) connections on the knot complement appears as vacua of T^DGG[M,K], whereas all of them are expected as vacua of the 6d theory, so T^DGG is not simply 'the' theory attached to the manifold. The corpus block states flatly that Z_{T[M^3]} on the squashed sphere EQUALS the state-integral invariant and lists as Open Question 1 'identify T[B_3] explicitly (DGG 2014 provides the construction)' -- this paper says that identification is qualified. Second, it identifies the gauge-theory operation corresponding to Dehn filling, i.e. how to close a knot complement, together with a topological criterion for the SU(2)/SO(3) enhancement of the U(1) flavour symmetry that the filling operation requires. It also shows all hyperbolic twist knots (the family containing 4_1, the corpus's muon anchor) exhibit an unexpected SU(3) enhancement. Corpus-grep over docs/audits/, content/, computations/, docs/coordination/: docs/duality-tracker.md D18 records the 3d-3d route as scaffold and the h^4 cross-check as not done, so the item is genuinely open and this paper bears on it.

keyResults.statement: T^DGG[M,K] realises only some subset of the irreducible flat SL(2,C) connections on the knot complement as its vacua, unlike the 6d theory T^6d[M,K]; the proposed relation T^6d -> T_irred -> T^DGG explains why T^DGG generically carries only a U(1) flavour symmetry.
keyResults.useForFolio: Qualifies conj:mirror-3d-3d-correspondence's stated equality between the squashed-sphere partition function and the state-integral invariant, and qualifies its Open Question 1: identifying T[B_3] by the DGG recipe does not by itself deliver the 6d object the conjecture's dictionary assumes.

keyResults.statement: A topological criterion on the knot complement for when the U(1)_{X_A} flavour symmetry of T^DGG enhances to SU(2)/SO(3).
keyResults.useForFolio: The precondition the corpus would have to check before applying any closing/filling operation to the Borromean complement; note the criterion is stated for a single torus boundary, and B_3 has three cusps, so transporting it is exactly the thing that would need checking.

keyResults.statement: Identification of the field-theoretic operation on T^DGG corresponding to Dehn filling, giving a construction of theories attached to closed 3-manifolds and predicting infinitely many 3d dualities from surgery calculus.
keyResults.useForFolio: The concrete route for Open Question 1 (identify T[B_3]); the corpus currently has only 'DGG 2014 provides the construction' with no closing procedure.

keyResults.statement: All hyperbolic twist knots give theories with SU(3) symmetry enhancement, unexpected from the 6d viewpoint.
keyResults.useForFolio: 4_1 is a twist knot and is the corpus's CAL-2 anchor; tbl:b1-hyperbolic-rows-theorem-table1-data indexes the twist-knot family K_n directly, so this is a concrete statement about the corpus's own knot family.

proposedActions.rationale: No ref() entry; the paper qualifies a claim conj:mirror-3d-3d-correspondence makes without qualification and answers its Open Question 1.

conj:mirror-3d-3d-correspondence cites dimofte-gaiotto-gukov2014, terashima-yamazaki2011, neumann-zagier1985 but not the paper that records the T^DGG vs T^6d flat-connection gap its dictionary depends on.

The T^DGG-realises-only-a-subset-of-flat-connections caveat should be stated in the folio rather than left implicit, since the conjecture's whole content is an equality of partition functions. NOT proposed as aid-proof: the enhancement criterion is stated for one torus boundary and B_3 has three cusps, so its applicability to the corpus's manifold is unchecked.
